title: The Fibonacci rule needs a negative weight in three dimensions
claim: With labels on edges, the Fibonacci rule on triangles and real Turaev-Viro-form weights with full support (per tau edge, per triangle with two or three tau edges, per admissible tetrahedron class, per vertex), the 2-3 and 1-4 identities force d t2 t3 W9 = 1, W8 = W9 t3/t2, W4^2 = W9 t3/t2^2, d^2 = d + 1 and W10 = -(W9 t2)^2 < 0: the all-tau tetrahedron carries a negative weight, so no non-negative weighting, in particular no count of hidden witnesses, makes the Fibonacci rule a three-manifold invariant in this form. An exact solution exists in Q(sqrt 5) (d = phi, W10 = -1/phi^2, vertex weight (5 - sqrt 5)/10), and unweighted counts fail.
failure_conditions: One of the identities used in the derivation is absent from the generated move identities.
A real full-support solution with a non-negative all-tau tetrahedron weight.
The stated exact solution fails an identity.
foundation_claim_scope: Polynomial identities of weighted state sums on triangulations; classical quantum topology cited as background. No physical claim.
